key_insight: Realistic piezoelectrically driven surface deformations can reshape near-wall turbulence, with spanwise waves producing the strongest drag reduction.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical route to active flow-control surfaces for lowering skin-friction drag in channels, pipelines, and other wall-bounded flows.
method: Performed direct numerical simulations of turbulent half-channel flow at friction Reynolds number Reτ=200.
Used finite-element analysis to model piezoelectric actuation of an aluminum sheet across practical voltage and frequency ranges.
Imposed the resulting wall deformations as moving boundary conditions to test upstream, downstream, and spanwise wave configurations.
evidence_signal: The simulations report maximum drag reductions of 1.6%, 5.4%, and 27.6% for upstream, downstream, and spanwise waves, respectively, over the explored actuation range.
watch_item: The strongest performance is shown at Reτ=200 and for modeled actuation conditions, so scalability to higher Reynolds numbers and real hardware durability remains uncertain.
paper_title: Direct numerical simulations of turbulent drag reduction via piezoelectric actuation
